summary: Capture, plan, prove and trim a checkpoint through a staging file on disk, so a checkpoint pass holds a fixed memory budget whatever the history, and a capture resumes after a restart (#2492).

replay.detail: No replay or rebuild. A checkpoint already sealed or verified continues; its next capture is staged.

schema.detail: No store schema change. The staging file is a scratch SQLite file in the checkpoint scratch directory (state_dir/checkpoint), deleted when its checkpoint is trimmed, superseded or has nothing left to capture.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and every digest (sealed, drop, retained, graph, reader) are unchanged: test builds plan every staged checkpoint with the previous in-memory planner as well and require identical plans, tombstone for tombstone, so members on either side of this change verify the same checkpoint.

compatibility.detail: No API or protocol change. `st replication checkpoint plan` stages into its own subdirectory and fails at once, instead of waiting, while another capture holds that directory.

manual.detail: No manual step. Members that set `[checkpoint] enabled = false` for #2492 can enable it again after this build is deployed.

recovery.detail: Deleting state_dir/checkpoint while the daemon is stopped is always safe; the next pass captures again.
